summary: extrahtml 0.1.2 fetches unpinned content from a pastebin-style host at install time; no library code shipped
details: The sdist's setup.py performs a top-level HTTP GET to https://plainraw.com/raw/99b69bda4246 on every install and PEP 517 build, then passes the response body to parseyaml.safe_load. The URL is an opaque short-ID on a pastebin-style raw-text host unrelated to the declared publisher/repository, is not pinned by hash or signature, and the content served there is mutable and attacker-controllable. The package otherwise ships no implementation: src/ contains only egg-info metadata, top_level.txt is empty, and SOURCES.txt lists no Python modules, so the README-advertised RequestsEngine/SeleniumEngine/PlaywrightEngine classes do not exist in the tarball. The only effect of installing this version is the install-time fetch and parse of remote content from a third-party paste host. Because no wheel is published, a default `pip install extrahtml` builds the sdist on every listed platform (Linux glibc/musl x86_64 and aarch64, macOS arm64/x86_64, Windows x86_64), so the fetch auto-executes on a default install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
